items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Another man, aged man, his name is Aaron and Cliff is on the piano and a man named Hank Larson on the drum... So you read and we're getting all these heads

ctx.x: Now was he using a -- what about -- do you know what -- was he playing any like whole-tone scales.

No, they were just simple scales. Pass it on the scales. He didn't move no further than that seventh or ninth, then he'd go into the diminish every now and then, but he'd just say right on that, that first -- fourth, fifth, of course, he might make a sixth come down, but you could understand anything he was doing, but he would do so much (unintelligible) and so then now I went -- then I got a job -- I'm a man, I'm getting a mustache and getting side-burns and things, so I got a job working with another man from…

So you read and we're getting all these heads and when your music started to change, had a thing called the "Louisiana Bobo," it had syncopation and Archie Bleyer was writing a lot of things that had syncopation, lot of syncopation and that's the first time we seen -- and it was a school for me.
